question.text: Aravalli Credit Fund is launching its second scheme and preparing the Private Placement Memorandum (PPM). As per SEBI Circular dated 21-Oct-2021, the PPM for a NEW scheme launch must be filed with SEBI:

answer.text: Directly by the Manager, without any intermediary.
Through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker who is NOT an associate of the AIF, sponsor, manager or trustee and who provides a due-diligence certificate.
By the Trustee, after Board approval.
By the custodian, who attaches the safekeeping undertaking.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I/DF6/P/CIR/2021/645 dated 21-Oct-2021 mandates that AIFs file PPM with SEBI through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker at the time of registration or launching new schemes. The merchant banker (a) conducts independent diligence of disclosures, (b) issues a due-diligence certificate and (c) must NOT be an associate of the AIF/sponsor/manager/trustee. Intimation of SPECIFIC changes in PPM terms can be filed directly (per SEBI circular dated 29-Apr-2024). The Trap: Option A ignores the MB-filing mandate. Option C confuses governance approval with the filing conduit. Option D invents a role for the custodian. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B tests PPM-filing awareness for distributors. XIX-C expects managers to know the NUANCE — new scheme launches go via MB, but specific term changes can be filed directly post-Apr-2024 circular. Manager's Pro-Tip: Hire a merchant banker who has done 20+ AIF PPMs — diligence is mechanical but SEBI queries are pattern-matched. A novice MB adds 4-6 weeks of iteration.
